owner: CHNragdoll (private repository owner and local data owner; approval decisions by the user)
purpose: Owner-controlled local migration and production of English vocabulary Anki packages; excludes unattended ingestion, hosted service use, and import into the owner's Anki collection by this release task.
distributionModel: Private GitHub source and authorized v3.0.0-rc.2 prerelease with source archive and owner study APKG; no hosted service or automatic updates.

repository.reviewMechanism: GitHub PR with independent review, one type label, one risk label, evidence and disposition; branch protection enforcement must be verified before integration. For v3.0.0-rc.1 only, owner approved the equivalent in docs/RELEASE.md on 2026-09-26; expires on completion or 2026-10-03.

environments: Development and verification: owner-controlled macOS, uv-locked Python 3.13 environment.
Local trial: owner-controlled macOS filesystem, SQLite and Anki APKG output; no daemon.
Anki desktop/mobile import compatibility: not yet executed; separate admission evidence required.
platforms: Python >=3.11 declared by package metadata; only observed runtimes count as verified.
macOS local trial; Anki desktop/mobile are downstream consumers, not yet verified.
architecture: Local CLI -> Excel/PDF/legacy SQLite/audio readers -> exact text and translation identity -> versioned SQLite -> quality check -> genanki APKG and HTML preview; optional explicit HTTPS enrich; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
stateModel: Old V2.0 inputs stay read-only. New SQLite schema v1 is authoritative for edited cards, sentences, translations, raw legacy snapshots and events; local copied audio, backup, CSV and APKG have separate roles. Restore only to a fresh path.
dataClassification: Private owner study data: workbook words/definitions, exam sentence text, manual translations, local audio and raw legacy rows.
Sensitive operational material: local paths, migration reports, content hashes, backup and export files.

Explicit enrichment requests transmit headwords; explicit example-speaker clicks transmit the English sentence to Youdao HTTPS, falling back to system speech. No automatic sentence request, raw SQLite or audio-library upload to providers. Private release APKG embeds study text and audio, excluded from Git history.
trustBoundaries: Local owner OS account and CLI/config/filesystem; no application login, remote service endpoint or session.
Read-only legacy SQLite/workbook/PDF/audio to separately owned new state.
Untrusted CSV and external dictionary HTTPS to validated local SQLite/audio.
Private GitHub source/release boundary; local data, backups, translations and generated artifacts excluded from source history.
riskRationale: Migration and translation misalignment can lose or misrepresent recoverable personal study content; generated packages can mislead learning. No public service, payment, privilege escalation, safety or regulated workflow is in scope. Backup and isolated restore reduce but do not eliminate impact.

applicability.rationale: The private repository and local data need one owner to decide scope, release, recovery, and retirement.
The local vocabulary-to-Anki trial has a specific owner consumer and excludes automatic Anki collection import.
The owner must retain private source, old inputs, new SQLite state, audio, lockfile, and restoration knowledge.
Migration and package errors can corrupt a recoverable study workflow, so project impact is classified R2.
First adoption requires all 92 catalog controls to be considered against this CLI, state, and release model.
The owner authorized implementation and private prerelease; merge and production decisions still need recorded authority.
Any future deviation from a mandatory gate needs scoped, expiring owner approval rather than a silent bypass.
The rebuild addresses legacy prefix false matches, duplicate merging, fragile translation alignment, and recovery risk.
The change boundaries include a new local pipeline, migrated state, and prerelease while keeping V2.0 inputs read-only.
Counts, stable IDs, exact matches, repeated runs, backup restore, package hashes, and client limits are observable.
Python, Anki format, old input integrity, private distribution, and no Anki import constrain the design.
The migration, translation, package, and release outcomes need links from acceptance to tests and artifacts.
Changing old-input write scope or adding client import would materially alter the authorized risk and acceptance.
The CLI crosses local file, private repository, optional dictionary HTTPS, and Anki package boundaries.
Input, parsing, state, translation, quality, packaging, and CLI modules have distinct change responsibilities.
TOML, Excel, PDF, CSV, SQLite, and APKG interfaces need declared inputs, errors, and version behavior.
Old files remain authoritative originals; the new SQLite database owns edits and generated packages are derived.
Malformed input, partial copies, stale CSV, failed network calls, and interrupted writes need explicit safe outcomes.
PyMuPDF, genanki, workbook parsing, and dictionary providers need pinning and a feasible replacement path.
Stable content IDs, raw-row retention, new-path restore, and no automatic Anki import are durable choices.
Code, schema, templates, lockfile, tests, and governance records must reproduce the private prerelease.
The rebuild is on a dedicated refactor branch and must preserve unrelated owner edits during integration.
Migration, parser, package, and governance commits should remain reviewable without raw data or credentials.
The authorized private GitHub PR must carry one refactor type, R2 rationale, evidence, and review disposition.
Local and PR checks must distinguish executed results from unrun Anki client import and release checks.
Merging the reviewed branch into main must leave a durable integration record and source ancestry.
The published tag, prerelease record, and review history must remain stable after distribution.
Migration, exact matching, translations, backup, package, and CLI behavior need different test boundaries.
Every acceptance item requires current evidence at the candidate version before a release claim.
The previous prefix and duplicate defects need repeatable regression checks, not only code inspection.
Python, TOML, JSON profile, schema, and package metadata have deterministic validation methods.
Parsers, state transactions, input validation, and package rendering warrant focused component tests.
SQLite-to-CSV, source-to-migration, and cards-to-APKG interactions require representative boundary checks.
A user must be able to install, migrate, review, export/import translations, check, and build locally.
Python >=3.11, macOS trial, Anki desktop/mobile, and package upgrades have distinct compatibility claims.
Fresh install, rerun migration, schema mismatch, restore, and rollback must be checked before delivery.
Workbook size, 1,960-card migration, PDF scans, media size, and memory use can affect local completion.
The CLI errors and browser preview are human interaction surfaces even without a hosted UI.
State loss is material, so a real restored database and digest/count comparison are required.
Local study content, old sources, CSV, generated cards, filesystem paths, and optional HTTPS are protected boundaries.

Access distinctions are the local OS owner and the private GitHub repository; no application-managed login/session exists. Verify private repository visibility, local-only CLI boundary and protected write targets.
Excel, PDF, HTML, CSV, TOML, and provider responses are untrusted inputs; Anki HTML output needs escaping.
Migration, import, extraction, enrichment, and build all change owner-controlled files or SQLite state.
Private repository release and optional provider access require source/artifact secret scanning even without app tokens.
Opt-in Oxford/Youdao lookups send headwords and need destination, HTTPS, timeout, size, and failure rules.
Original exam text, translations, workbook definitions, audio, reports, and hashes have different exposure needs.
Locally edited translations and study material can be private; storage, transfer, retention, and deletion need policy.
Legacy files, PDF, MP3, backup paths, CSV, and APKG output expose parser and filesystem boundaries.
Offline-by-default, independent output paths, and fail-closed integrity and alignment checks are material defaults.
Dependency and code findings for a distributed private prerelease need severity and disposition records.
Loss or exposure of the local database or private repository requires owner containment and recovery steps.
Runtime packages, Python/uv tools, Anki format library, and dictionary providers form the dependency inventory.
Exact package pins and uv lock hashes are needed to reproduce migration and generated APKG behavior.
PyPI packages and dictionary endpoints need authoritative source and mirror provenance decisions.
The private source and possible APKG assets distribute third-party code/derived assets with license obligations.
Pinned Python libraries and runtime need version-specific vulnerability review for operational use.
Unreviewed library upgrades could change parsing, database, HTML, or package output.
The APKG must be tied to the integrated source, lockfile, local inputs, tools, and build report.
Each PDF, workbook, HTTP, and packaging dependency adds maintenance and replacement cost.
New SQLite is authoritative for edited cards/translations; old V2.0 remains immutable source evidence.
SQLite user_version, CSV header/hash, workbook columns, and APKG fields define persistent/exchanged formats.
Cards and sentences use content-derived IDs so order changes cannot silently reassign translations.
Migration, wordbook, PDF, and CSV changes require validation, backup, transaction, and repeat-run behavior.
The old-to-new schema transition and future SQLite versions require migration and recovery paths.
Raw legacy rows, local backups, reports, and CSV exports need owner-set retention and verified deletion.
SQLite, CSV, TOML, audio, and package files must be owner-exportable without provider dependence.
Losing local translations/audio is material; backup integrity and a restored copy need evidence.
The private prerelease needs one unique v3.0.0-rc.1 identity tied to Python 3.0.0rc1 metadata.
The prerelease needs human notes covering fixes, migration, limitations, and actual checks.
An annotated tag on the integrated main commit is the declared immutable release reference.
A GitHub prerelease record must disclose version, scope, verification, compatibility, and rollback.
The source archive and optional APKG must be checked against the tag and recorded hashes.
The authorized release still needs a conformance/gate decision with unresolved checks visible.
Consumers moving from V2.0 need isolated migration and restored-path rollback instructions.
PR, merge commit, version, tag, prerelease, build report, and hashes must refer to one source state.
Candidate, delivered prerelease, and production/Anki-client admission are separate readiness claims.
The owner needs reproducible private-source installation, configuration, build, update, and removal steps.
The local macOS environment, TOML paths, optional network, and private GitHub authority must be documented.
CLI reports, SQLite events, failed-command output, and evidence retention are the local observability surface.
Network request limits, PDF/workbook size, disk space, backup growth, and stop conditions affect use.
The owner depends on continuity of study data and needs recovery objectives and exercised restoration.
Private prerelease users need owner issue intake, version support, severity, and update expectations.
Migration and subsequent local state changes need backup, validation, stop, and manual rollback procedures.
Retirement must preserve/export study state, close provider use, handle private access, and delete retained copies.
A stable entry point must point consumers to setup, architecture, operations, and release evidence.
Install, test, migrate, backup, restore, build, release, and retirement commands need executable instructions.
Test, migration, source-hash, build, and release evidence need version, environment, time, and location.
Old trial passes cannot substantiate a changed candidate after code, input, or dependency drift.
Version strings, counts, paths, readiness, release notes, and APKG hashes must agree.
A browser preview or APKG build cannot be reported as a tested Anki desktop/mobile import.
The owner needs enough setup, state, recovery, and release knowledge outside this conversation.
R2 risk, raw retention, exact matching, and private prerelease choices need retained rationale.

releasePolicy: Authorized v3.0.0-rc.2 delivery: real private GitHub PR from fix/template-parity, one type:bug and risk:R2 label, latest Python 3.11/3.13 CI and independent review, explicit merge commit into main, annotated tag v3.0.0-rc.2, private prerelease with source/APKG hashes and scoped gate evidence. Inspect live branch protection; rc.1 approval is expired and cannot authorize rc.2 equivalent control. See docs/RELEASE_RC2.md for current decision and docs/RELEASE.md for historical rc.1. No production or full Anki GUI admission claim.
recoveryPolicy: Keep original V2.0 inputs unchanged and hash-verified; create SQLite online backup before state writes, verify integrity, restore only to a new file, compare counts/content digest/sample IDs and audio before manually changing config. Owner records retention, separated copy and recovery exercise before operational admission.
evidenceReusePolicy: Reuse a prior PASS only when scope, source commit, relevant inputs and hashes, dependencies/lockfile, runtime environment and decision are unchanged; schema, migration, permissions, network or packaging changes invalidate relevant evidence. PRIOR_PASS and NOT_RUN never become current PASS by inference.
